summary:
Earth Through Time is an interactive 3D geospatial platform designed to explore how our planet has changed over time and understand how it may evolve in the future.

By combining scientific datasets from NASA Earthdata and JPL, including MODIS, AIRS, GISTEMP v4 and MUR SST, with environmental information from institutions such as CSIC and MITECO, our platform brings together different sources of information in a unified interface.

Users can explore environmental variables such as temperature, vegetation, ocean dynamics, ice melt and ecosystem vulnerability through an interactive 3D globe and a timeline spanning historical, present-day and future scenarios. The platform also incorporates statistical trend detection to help identify and understand significant environmental changes.

Earth Through Time addresses the challenge by transforming complex scientific data into an accessible, visual and interactive tool for exploring Earth system trends. It aims to support scientific research, environmental management, conservation planning and education.

The past explains us. The present alerts us. The future prepares us.
details:
Earth Through Time is an interactive 3D geospatial platform that allows users to explore, analyze and understand changes in Earth's environmental systems over time. It combines scientific datasets from multiple institutions into a unified interface, transforming complex environmental information into an accessible and interactive experience.

How does it work?

Users interact with a 3D globe to select geographical locations, explore environmental variables and investigate changes across different time periods. The platform includes a catalogue of 17 environmental variables and provides historical data, current observations and future climate projections where available. Users can also explore natural events, compare environmental trends and generate reports for specific geographical cases.

Our data sources include NASA POWER (using MERRA-2 and CERES-related variables), NASA GISTEMP, NASA EONET, NASA GIBS, MODIS vegetation data, NOAA precipitation and sea-level datasets, NSIDC sea-ice records and NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate projections.

Technology and development

The frontend was developed using React 19 and TypeScript 7, with Vite 8 as the development and build tool. The interactive globe is powered by globe.gl and Three.js, using WebGL for 3D rendering, while Apache ECharts provides interactive charts and statistical visualizations.

The backend uses Node.js serverless functions deployed on Vercel. A Python-based data pipeline, built with libraries such as NumPy, xarray, SciPy, Matplotlib and Pillow, downloads, processes, prepares and validates scientific datasets before they are integrated into the application.

One of our main technical contributions is a custom statistical engine written in TypeScript. It implements the Mann-Kendall trend test, Sen's slope estimator and linear regression, alongside confidence intervals and autocorrelation checks. This allows users to investigate not only what is changing, but also the magnitude and statistical significance of environmental trends.

Benefits and intended impact

Earth Through Time aims to make scientific data easier to understand and use. It can support environmental research, climate monitoring, conservation planning, decision-making and education. Potential users include research institutions, environmental agencies, protected-area managers, public administrations and educational organizations.

Creativity and innovation

Our main innovation is bringing global environmental datasets, geographical exploration, temporal visualization and statistical trend analysis together in a single platform. Rather than simply displaying environmental maps, Earth Through Time helps users investigate relationships between environmental variables, identify significant trends and explore possible future scenarios.

Throughout development, we considered scientific reliability, data availability, geographical and temporal coverage, uncertainty, performance, accessibility and usability. We also designed the architecture to work without mandatory API keys or external AI services, keeping the scientific calculations independent from AI-generated text.

Our vision is simple: the past explains us, the present alerts us, and the future prepares us.

Live demonstration

Watch our demonstration video to see Earth Through Time in action, including its interactive 3D globe, environmental data exploration, temporal analysis and statistical tools.
